From 1214bf28965ceaf584fb20d357731264dd2e10e1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pengpeng Hou <pengpeng@iscas.ac.cn>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 13:40:16 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] greybus: gb-beagleplay: bound bootloader receive buffering

cc1352_bootloader_rx() appends each serdev chunk into the fixed
rx_buffer before parsing bootloader packets. The helper can keep
leftover bytes between callbacks and may receive multiple packets in one
callback, so a single count value is not constrained by one packet
length.

Check that the incoming chunk fits in the remaining receive buffer space
before memcpy(). If it does not, drop the staged data and consume the
bytes instead of overflowing rx_buffer.

Fixes: 0cf7befa3ea2 ("greybus: gb-beagleplay: Add firmware upload API")
Cc: stable <stable@kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Pengpeng Hou <pengpeng@iscas.ac.cn>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260402054016.38587-1-pengpeng@iscas.ac.cn
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/greybus/gb-beagleplay.c b/drivers/greybus/gb-beagleplay.c
index 305066febbe7..244966d56c9b 100644
--- a/drivers/greybus/gb-beagleplay.c
+++ b/drivers/greybus/gb-beagleplay.c
@@ -623,6 +623,13 @@ static size_t cc1352_bootloader_rx(struct gb_beagleplay *bg, const u8 *data,
 		return count;
 	}
 
+	if (count > sizeof(bg->rx_buffer) - bg->rx_buffer_len) {
+		dev_warn(&bg->sd->dev,
+			 "dropping oversized bootloader receive chunk");
+		bg->rx_buffer_len = 0;
+		return count;
+	}
+
 	memcpy(bg->rx_buffer + bg->rx_buffer_len, data, count);
 	bg->rx_buffer_len += count;
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

- **drivers/greybus/gb-beagleplay.c**  
  In the function `cc1352_bootloader_rx()`, a new guard condition was added *before* the `memcpy()` that copies received data into `bg->rx_buffer`. The check verifies that the incoming chunk size (`count`) does not exceed the remaining space in `bg->rx_buffer` (i.e., `sizeof(bg->rx_buffer) - bg->rx_buffer_len`).  
  - If the chunk *fits*, the previous behavior continues (copy and update length).  
  - If the chunk *does not fit*, a warning is logged, the receive buffer length is reset to 0 (discarding any partially staged data), and the function returns `count` to indicate the bytes have been consumed (but not stored), preventing an overflow.

### Relationship Between Modifications

The single change in `gb-beagleplay.c` addresses a potential buffer overflow vulnerability in the bootloader receive path. The fix ensures that even when multiple packets arrive in one callback or leftover bytes remain from a previous callback, the fixed-size `rx_buffer` is never written beyond its capacity. Instead of overflowing, the driver discards any pending data and resynchronizes by consuming the oversized chunk, thus maintaining protocol safety without altering any other logic.
